intro: The ChatGPT Mac app has no live Share Screen button that I could confirm in its documentation. Instead, show ChatGPT one window at a time, using Screen context in Settings > Voice or an Appshot made by pressing both Command keys.
tldr: The ChatGPT Mac app has no live Share Screen button that I could confirm. Third-party guides tie live sharing to the phone app.
Voice Screen context: turn it on in Settings > Voice, then say “Take a look at this.” You get one look per phrase.
Appshots: bring a window forward and press both Command keys. Allow Screen & System Audio Recording and Accessibility first.
Blocked or missing features? Take a screenshot, then attach the image to your chat.
Check your version with ChatGPT > Check for Updates before you troubleshoot. Older builds may lack these features.

blocks.text: Most people who ask this want ChatGPT to see one window while they talk or type. That is a smaller job than full screen sharing. The Mac app handles it in three ways, and each suits a different kind of question. This guide covers all three, then the permissions, the limits, and the fixes people need most.
Does ChatGPT on Mac have a live Share Screen button?

Not in any source I could open. Third-party guides say OpenAI documents live screen sharing only in the iOS and Android Advanced Voice experience. A MakeUseOf guide dated February 20, 2025 walks through that phone flow. It uses the voice icon, a three-dot menu, and a Share Screen option. Those steps belong to the phone app, so they will not match your Mac.

An OpenAI Developer Community thread asked for screen viewing in the macOS app. It opened on May 26, 2024. The latest reply came on November 28, 2025, and no OpenAI staff member answered in the thread. Users there suggested workarounds, including the iPadOS app. A request open for over a year with no official reply is a sign to plan around the feature.

blocks.title: Menu names can change
blocks.text: The menu labels here come from OpenAI’s training pages and from third-party guides. OpenAI’s help center did not load during checks. If a label on your Mac differs, update ChatGPT first, then look again.
Option 1: Voice Screen context, the closest thing to sharing

Voice Screen context comes closest to sharing. You turn it on once in Settings > Voice. Then you start a voice chat and say “Take a look at this.” ChatGPT looks at the window in front of you. It does not keep watching. Each phrase gives ChatGPT one look at the screen at that moment.

Setup takes a few minutes. The first time, ChatGPT asks for microphone access. You also choose a voice and review Screen context. OpenAI’s Voice walkthrough lists Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, and Enterprise plans. It also lists Remote on iOS, after you pair your computer. Free is not on that list, so check your plan before you spend time on setup.

Here is a worked example. Say a sales chart is open in Numbers, and you want the drop explained. Bring that window to the front. Start voice mode, then say “Take a look at this.” Ask, “Which month fell the most?” If you switch to another chart, say the phrase again. The earlier look does not update on its own.
Voice works best for spoken questions about one window. For typed follow-ups, Appshots is the better fit.
Option 2: Appshots with both Command keys

An Appshot captures the frontmost window and sends it to ChatGPT. Bring the window forward and click it first, because the click decides which window is in front. Then press both Command keys together. You can set a custom hotkey in ChatGPT settings instead. After the capture, ask your task about the appshot. The docs say ChatGPT also gets the available text from that window, not only the picture.

The destination setting decides where the Appshot lands. The three choices are Current chat, New chat, and Automatic. Automatic is the default. Under Automatic, an Appshot starts a new chat unless you interacted with a chat in the last 60 seconds. If you did, it joins that chat. Consecutive Appshots go to the same chat.

Pick the setting that fits your habit. If you work in one long chat, Current chat keeps every capture in that thread. If you ask unrelated questions all day, New chat keeps each capture clean. Automatic suits most people, but it can surprise you when you switch tasks quickly.
Option 3: Take a screenshot and upload it

The plain route is the fallback when the other two do not work for you. Open Spotlight with ⌘ Space, type Screenshot, and press Return. Choose the window or the area you need. Then drag the capture into the chat box, or attach it with the paperclip. ChatGPT sees the file you attach, and nothing more.

Use this route when you need one area of the screen, or when you want full control over what ChatGPT sees. You also choose the moment. The cost is effort. You capture again each time the screen changes. If you prefer to paste, copy the capture and press ⌘ V in the chat box.

blocks.text: Permissions you must allow on your Mac

Appshots and Voice Screen context need two permissions. Open System Settings > Privacy & Security. Screen & System Audio Recording lets ChatGPT capture an image of the frontmost window. Accessibility lets it read the available text from that window. If either one is off, the feature can seem to do nothing.

Check both before you troubleshoot anything else. macOS may show a prompt you missed, and that prompt waits in System Settings until you answer it. Some older macOS versions may label the first permission Screen Recording. I could not confirm that label, so look for the closest match in the list.

The order below works well. Allow Screen & System Audio Recording first, then Accessibility. Quit ChatGPT, reopen it, and try again. The OpenAI troubleshooting steps for Appshots end with the same restart.
Google Docs, Gmail, Sheets, and Slides limits

OpenAI’s Appshots page warns about four Google apps: Google Docs, Gmail, Google Sheets, and Google Slides. For these, ChatGPT may receive only the visible screenshot. It may not get the full document or the text that is off screen.

Take a long contract open in Google Docs as an example. If the clause you care about sits off screen, the Appshot may miss it. Scroll until the clause is visible, capture again, then ask. Keep sensitive content out of view unless your question needs it.
Mistakes people make

items: Expecting a live feed. Voice and Appshots capture one moment each. Ask again after the window changes.
Skipping the permissions. Appshots can seem to do nothing until Screen & System Audio Recording and Accessibility are on.
Confusing screen sharing with a chat link. A share link sends a conversation, not your screen. For that route, read [how to share a chat in ChatGPT on Mac](/how-to/share-a-chat-in-chatgpt).
Sending an Appshot to the wrong chat. Automatic joins a chat you used in the last 60 seconds. Switch to New chat when you want a fresh thread.
Sharing more than you meant. The capture includes whatever text the window holds, so close private tabs first.
Running an old build. Voice Screen context depends on a recent desktop release, so update before you start.

blocks.text: Plans, versions, and the app name

The Voice walkthrough lists Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, and Enterprise. The Appshots docs do not name a plan. They do say your organization must allow Appshots, so a work account may block the feature even on a paid plan. Ask your admin if the feature is missing.

A third-party summary says Voice Screen context shipped in desktop release 26.715 on July 23, 2026. I could not confirm that date in OpenAI’s changelog. Check your version with ChatGPT > Check for Updates. The download page gives no version number, so the update check is the reliable test.
The old app was renamed ChatGPT Classic. If you see that name in Applications, update or reinstall before you follow these steps.
When macOS blocks the app or chats go missing

If macOS says ChatGPT is damaged or cannot be verified, do not choose Open Anyway. A FelloAI guide says old builds signed with a revoked certificate are blocked from June 2026. Quit the app, move ChatGPT.app to the Trash, then reinstall from chatgpt.com/download.

If chats or Projects seem to be missing after an update, a FelloAI guide says a July 9, 2026 rebuild hid some items until a July 16 build restored access. Update first, then check Archived chats in Settings.
Privacy before you share a window

Anything visible in the window can reach ChatGPT. An Appshot sends the captured image and the available text. Voice Screen context sends the frontmost window when you say the phrase. A screenshot upload sends the file you attach, and nothing else.
Close private messages, password manager windows, and bank pages before you start. Look at the window once more right before you capture, because a notification can slide in on top.
Next steps

If your question is about a file rather than a window, read [how to attach a file in ChatGPT](/how-to/attach-a-file-in-chatgpt). For spoken questions after setup, read [how to use voice mode in ChatGPT on Mac](/how-to/use-voice-mode-in-chatgpt). faq.question: Is there a Share Screen button in ChatGPT on Mac?
faq.answer: Not in any source I could open. Live Share Screen is described for the phone app’s Advanced Voice. On a Mac, use Voice Screen context, Appshots, or a screenshot upload.

faq.question: What happens when I say Take a look at this?
faq.answer: ChatGPT takes one look at the frontmost window through Voice Screen context. It does not watch the screen all the time. Say the phrase again after the window changes.

faq.question: Does Appshots work on the free plan?
faq.answer: The Appshots docs do not name a plan. The Voice walkthrough lists Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, and Enterprise, and free is not on that list. Check your plan in your account before you set up either feature.

faq.question: Can ChatGPT see my whole desktop at once?
faq.answer: Not with the options described here. Voice and Appshots both work on the frontmost window. To include a second window, bring it forward first, or capture a screenshot that shows both.

faq.question: Why does Appshots need Accessibility permission?
faq.answer: Accessibility lets ChatGPT read the available text from the window. Screen & System Audio Recording lets it capture the image. You need both for the full result.

faq.question: Why did my Appshot start a new chat?
faq.answer: Under Automatic, an Appshot starts a new chat unless you interacted with a chat in the last 60 seconds. Set the destination to Current chat or New chat if you want more control.

faq.question: Can I share a chat link instead?
faq.answer: Yes, but a chat link shares a conversation, not your screen. Right-click the chat name in the sidebar, choose Share chat, then Share Link. Chats inside a Project cannot be shared until you move them out.

steps.name: Update ChatGPT for Mac
steps.text: Open the ChatGPT menu and choose Check for Updates. Let the update finish, then reopen the app. The features in this guide need a current build.
steps.tip: If Applications still shows ChatGPT Classic, you have the older app. Reinstall from chatgpt.com/download.

steps.name: Open Voice settings
steps.text: Open Settings from the ChatGPT menu, then select Voice. This is where Screen context lives.

steps.name: Turn on Screen context
steps.text: Find Screen context in the Voice settings and turn it on. On first use, review it along with the microphone and voice choices.
steps.tip: Voice is listed for Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, and Enterprise plans.

steps.name: Allow Screen & System Audio Recording
steps.text: When macOS asks, allow Screen & System Audio Recording for ChatGPT. If you missed the prompt, open this pane and switch ChatGPT on.

steps.name: Allow Accessibility
steps.text: In the same Privacy & Security pane, open Accessibility and switch ChatGPT on. Appshots need this to read the window’s text.
steps.tip: Quit and reopen ChatGPT after you change either permission.

steps.name: Start a voice chat
steps.text: Select the Voice icon before you send your first message. The chat opens in voice mode, so you can speak your question.

steps.name: Say the phrase
steps.text: With the window you want in front, say “Take a look at this.” ChatGPT looks at the frontmost window once. Then ask your question out loud.
steps.tip: Say the phrase again after the window changes. Each look is a snapshot, not a live feed.

steps.name: Check the Appshots hotkey
steps.text: Open ChatGPT settings and look for the Appshots section. The default trigger is both Command keys. You can set a custom hotkey there instead.
steps.tip: The docs do not name the exact pane, so look for an Appshots section.

steps.name: Choose the Appshot destination
steps.text: Pick Current chat, New chat, or Automatic. Automatic joins a chat you used in the last 60 seconds, and starts a new chat otherwise.
steps.tip: Pick New chat if you want every capture in a fresh thread.

steps.name: Bring the window to the front
steps.text: Click the window you want so it is frontmost. Only the frontmost window is captured, so the click matters.

steps.name: Press both Command keys
steps.text: Press both Command keys together. If ChatGPT asks for permission, finish that setup first. Then ask your task about the appshot.
steps.tip: If nothing happens, check System Settings for a permission prompt you missed.

steps.name: Capture with Screenshot
steps.text: If Appshots are not available, open Spotlight, type Screenshot, and press Return. Capture the window or the area you need.
steps.tip: Keep the capture visible so you can check it before you attach it.

steps.name: Attach the image and ask
steps.text: Drag the image into the chat box, or attach it with the paperclip. Type your question, then send it.
steps.tip: For more on attaching files, read the attach a file guide in Next steps.

troubleshooting.problem: The Screen context switch is missing
troubleshooting.fix: Update ChatGPT with ChatGPT > Check for Updates. A third-party summary ties the Voice option to desktop release 26.715, from July 23, 2026, so older builds may not have it.

troubleshooting.problem: Appshots or Screen context does nothing
troubleshooting.fix: Check System Settings for a permission prompt you missed. Confirm Screen & System Audio Recording and Accessibility are on for ChatGPT. Then quit and reopen the app, and try again.

troubleshooting.problem: An Appshot joined the wrong chat
troubleshooting.fix: Automatic joins a chat you used in the last 60 seconds. Switch the destination to New chat, or wait a minute before you capture.

troubleshooting.problem: macOS says ChatGPT is damaged or cannot be verified
troubleshooting.fix: Do not choose Open Anyway. Quit ChatGPT, move ChatGPT.app to the Trash, then reinstall from chatgpt.com/download. A FelloAI guide describes this fix.

troubleshooting.problem: Chats or Projects disappeared after an update
troubleshooting.fix: Update with ChatGPT > Check for Updates, then check Archived chats in Settings. A third-party guide says a July 16, 2026 build restored access.

troubleshooting.problem: Google Docs content is cut short in an Appshot
troubleshooting.fix: The Appshots docs say these apps may send only the visible screenshot. Scroll to the part you need, then capture again.
